skill.name: executing-plans
skill.description: Execute implementation plans through structured batches, verification steps, blocker handling, and review checkpoints.
skill.summary: Guides agents through plan execution with batches, verification, and user feedback checkpoints.
skill.author: DMJGilbert

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting and ordinary planning prose in SKILL.md. No evidence of command execution, network reconnaissance, prompt injection, or malicious intent was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 33 uses Markdown inline code around the status value in_progress. It is instructional prose, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 36 uses Markdown inline code around the status value completed. There is no executable command or command injection surface.
Lines 42 through 56 are a fenced Markdown example for a batch completion report. The backticks delimit documentation, not code execution.
Line 77 says plan gaps can block progress. This is normal project-management guidance and contains no network probing or reconnaissance instruction.

content.value_statement: Implementation plans can lose quality when tasks are rushed or batched without checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through small batches, verification, reporting, and user checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Reviews an implementation plan before work starts and raises ambiguities.
Creates tracked tasks from an accepted plan.
Executes work in small batches with a default of three tasks.
Runs specified verification before marking tasks complete.
Reports completed tasks, verification results, issues, and readiness for feedback.
Stops for blockers, unclear instructions, repeated failures, or critical issues.
limitations: Requires a separate implementation plan before use.
Does not define project-specific test commands unless the plan includes them.
Relies on the agent environment for task tracking support.
Does not replace human review for high-risk changes.

use_cases.title: Implement a prepared feature plan
use_cases.description: Turn an approved plan into tracked batches with verification after each task group.

use_cases.title: Coordinate review checkpoints
use_cases.description: Pause after each batch so stakeholders can review progress and request changes.

use_cases.title: Control high-risk project changes
use_cases.description: Use smaller batches and explicit blocker handling for migrations, refactors, or critical fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Start plan execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin from a complete plan document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the executing-plans skill on this plan: [paste plan]. Review it first, create tasks, and start with the default batch size.

prompt_templates.title: Execute with checkpoints
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep the user involved between batches.
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute this plan in batches of three tasks. After each batch, report completed work, verification results, issues, and wait for my feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Handle uncertain plan details
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a plan before implementation when details may be incomplete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this implementation plan before starting. Identify ambiguities, blockers, and risky assumptions. Ask me for clarification before creating tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Run high-risk execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Use stricter controls for risky changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute this high-risk plan one task at a time. Verify each task before continuing, stop on repeated failures, and report every blocker immediately.

output_examples.input: Execute a plan with three simple implementation tasks.
output_examples.output: The agent reviews the plan, creates three tracked tasks, completes the batch, reports each verification result, and asks for feedback.

output_examples.input: Execute a plan that contains unclear migration requirements.
output_examples.output: The agent stops before implementation, lists the unclear requirements, explains the blocker, and asks targeted questions.
The agent reduces the batch size to one task, verifies each change, reports issues early, and pauses before continuing.

best_practices: Provide a complete plan with clear tasks, verification steps, and expected outcomes.
Use smaller batches for complex, risky, or cross-module changes.
Review each batch report before allowing the next batch to begin.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when no implementation plan exists.
Do not skip verification steps to finish batches faster.
Do not continue through unresolved blockers or repeated failures.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an agent through a prepared plan using batches, verification steps, reports, and user checkpoints.

faq.question: Does it write implementation plans?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to execute an existing plan after the plan has been reviewed.

faq.question: What is the default batch size?
faq.answer: The skill uses three tasks by default, with smaller batches for complex or high-risk work.

faq.question: When should the agent stop?
faq.answer: The agent should stop for blockers, unclear instructions, repeated verification failures, or unresolved critical issues.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when task tracking and verification are available.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to run specified verifications and the full test suite after all tasks are complete.
